In the latest survey from the American Association of Individual Investors (AAII), just 34.7% of individual investors said they were bullish on stocks over the next six months—below the historical average for the fourth consecutive week.

Just one week earlier, bearish sentiment had been above its historical average for 27 consecutive weeks. And when AAII asked members about other investors’ attitudes, nearly half said they thought everyone else was too bullish. [...] Simply put, investors haven’t collectively thrown caution out the window.

And historically, that can be a much healthier environment for stocks than it feels.
